slides.headline: From text to vectors
slides.body: The tokenizer splits text into tokens (words, subwords, or characters). Then the embedding layer maps each token to a dense vector representation, capturing semantic meaning.

slides.body: Attention mechanisms are permutation-invariant—they don't know position. Positional encoding injects token order information, allowing the model to understand sequence.

slides.headline: The core mechanism: self-attention
slides.body: Self-attention computes relationships between every pair of tokens in the context. Using query, key, and value vectors, it determines relevance and produces context-aware representations.
